svg.text: ZERADO — THE MIGRATION DECISION AT START-UP · SHEET 4
there is no DBA. The program migrates its own file, or it refuses and says why
A fresh install runs the SAME
A newer binary wrote this file.
but the file is not empty.
The transaction rolls back. The file is byte-identical to what it was.
The program REFUSES to run and names three things: the migration that failed,
the error, and the backup path if one was taken.
There is no half-applied version, because the bookkeeping INSERT is inside
the same transaction as the DDL it records.
clean shutdown: wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE), then close -> exactly one file
FORWARD-ONLY. There are no down migrations: a mistake is corrected by a NEW migration, never by reversing one.
A RELEASED MIGRATION IS IMMUTABLE. Editing 0001 after a release means two files claim version 1 and disagree about what it did.
EVERY PATH ENDS SOMEWHERE NAMED. The program opens the file, or it refuses and says which version wrote it and which one is running.
Silently proceeding against a schema you do not understand is how one file becomes two incompatible files.
Forward-only. Every path ends in an open file or a named refusal.
